sections.html:
Utah's far southwest corner, right against Arizona, is home to St. George, seat of Washington County. Interstate 15 passes through at 2,530 feet, around 118 miles from Las Vegas and 300 from Salt Lake City. About 77 square miles of Mojave Desert edge lie beneath the Pine Valley Mountains, and both the Virgin River and Santa Clara River cross the valley.

The population went from 49,728 in 2000 to 95,342 in 2020, with an estimate of 108,713 for July 1, 2025, which means plenty of the housing is newly built. For 2020 to 2024, owner-occupied homes have a median value of $496,100, and 66.7% are lived in by their owners. Your own house could price higher or lower than that survey figure.

The city skews older than most of Utah, since 21.8% of residents are 65 or over. Downsizers and heirs show up often among sellers.

Buyers inspect for heat above all. Averages run from 42.1 degrees in December to 87.8 in July. Roughly 60 afternoons a year hit 100 or more, and the all-time high was 118 on July 4, 2007. Another 60 mornings or so fall to freezing, so poorly insulated pipes remain a worry.

  • Air conditioners and roofs wear fastest, and inspectors ask how old they are.
  • Stucco, window seals and flat roofs can hide sun damage that the curb view misses.
  • Near the Santa Clara River or a wash, expect questions about drainage because of the January 2005 flood.

With a 1992 earthquake and that flood both on the record, look into your lot's flood and soil history before pricing.

Water is a live issue across Washington County. A 2022 ordinance from the Washington County Water Conservancy District bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial, institutional and industrial sites and caps grass at new homes. Cities do the enforcing, from water-waste complaints to metering data to penalties.

Heavy water users have paid an added fee since 2023, which funds rebates for swapping grass for water-efficient plantings. The district projected savings of nearly 11 billion gallons over ten years. With a large lawn on your lot, find out from the city or your water provider what applies before putting money into landscaping.

Interstate 15 runs northeast to southwest through the city. State Route 7, the Southern Parkway, runs east and west along the south edge, and SR-8, SR-34 and SR-18 also serve the city. The regional airport on the southeast side has flights on American, Delta and United, all flown by SkyWest.

Washington County School District high schools include Desert Hills, Dixie, Pine View, Snow Canyon and Crimson Cliffs. A family moving in often asks first which one a house feeds, so verify the boundary for your address.

November 30 is the yearly due date in Washington County, notice or no notice. The county treasurer treats tax as a lien on the property and not on a person, which is why an unpaid bill follows the house to a new owner. At closing the title company splits the bill, and the settlement statement lists each side's portion.

StepDetail
Due dateNovember 30
Late penalty2.5% or $10, whichever is greater
Reduced penalty1% if everything is paid by January 31
Partial payments$10 or more per parcel, accepted any time
Further appealUtah State Tax Commission, Form TC-194, filed with the auditor within 30 days of the Board of Equalization ruling
Tax saleEach May, for properties delinquent at least five years

The treasurer is at 111 East Tabernacle St., St. George, (435) 301-7720, and the auditor is at (435) 301-7220. Utah gives a 45% exemption on a primary residence, up to one acre. Rental homes can qualify, while vacation homes and time-shares do not, so a second home in St. George is taxed on its full value. Ask the Washington County assessor how your parcel is classified.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or out-of-state house
sections.html: Out-of-state heirs sell a lot of St. George houses. The to-do list matches anyone else's: a current payoff from the treasurer, a lien check, and access for the title company. Cash makes remote handling realistic, with no showings to arrange in July heat and no repair list to manage from afar.

Start with a description of the house and your timeline. Our offer comes back, and you can turn it down. Put it next to a listing's net after agent fees, repairs and months of upkeep. Say yes, and a title company draws up the paperwork, clears any lien or mortgage, splits the tax bill and pays you the remainder.

The purchase is as-is, so no roof repair, AC replacement or yard staging is needed, even with deferred repairs, heat-damaged roofs or tenants in place. Take photo ID, payoff details, your newest tax notice and the keys to signing.

sections.h2: Listing, selling yourself or taking cash
sections.html:
Putting the house on the market can bring a better price if it shows well and the AC and roof are sound, though you will face summer showings, an inspection and repair requests. Going it alone saves the agent fee but hands you the pricing, advertising and buyer screening. Cash gives up some price in return for speed and certainty, which suits tenants, a failing roof or AC, or a thirsty lawn.

Request an offer and do the math yourself. It obligates you to nothing and gives you a concrete figure to set against a listing.

sections.h2: If you own a second home or rental
sections.html: A vacation home or time-share gets no exemption, so its bill runs higher than a primary residence's. Let the title company know which category the parcel falls into so that closing proration comes out right, and check with the assessor if you are unsure. Rental homes can qualify, so landlords should confirm the parcel's classification before the bill is divided. If tenants live in the house, bring the lease to the signing.

What sellers tell us tends to be practical: a worn-out air conditioner or roof, a yard that is expensive to water, an heir living in another state, or a house nobody wants to tour in July. Cash skips the prep, so none of those has to be fixed before you sell.

faqs.q: How many people live in St. George, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 108,713 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 95,342 in the 2020 census. The city is the largest in Washington County and the county seat.

faqs.q: When are St. George property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property taxes in Washington County are due November 30 each year. After that date they are delinquent, and Utah law adds a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, reduced to 1% if paid by January 31.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a St. George house sells?
faqs.a: The title company prorates the bill at closing, so the seller covers the days they owned the house and the buyer covers the rest. The lien follows the property, so any unpaid balance must be settled at or before closing.

faqs.q: Does St. George have special water or landscaping rules?
faqs.a: Yes. A 2022 Washington County Water Conservancy District ordinance limits grass at new homes and bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial and industrial sites. Cities enforce it, and a heavy water-use fee began in 2023. Ask the city how it applies to your lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell a St. George house that needs repairs or has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, including ones with deferred repairs, heat-damaged roofs or tenants in place. Tell us about the house and we will give you an offer you are free to decline.
